primary_work.title: Causal Representation Learning Made Identifiable by Grouping of Observational Variables

rejected_claims: known observational grouping is itself a novel language contribution
language that merely restates grouping metadata identifies latent intervention targets
group-shuffle self-supervision alone establishes raw-language equivalence identification
remaining_candidate: After applying intervention-based, general-environment, trajectory-local, multimodal partial-sharing, and known-observational-grouping identifiability criteria, determine whether an externally anchored population language channel can jointly identify an otherwise unknown observational grouping and a residual latent intervention-target partition.
counterexample: If language-derived grouping G=q(L)=r(X) is already measurable from non-language observations X, then I(P;G|X)=0 and adding G cannot distinguish candidate latent partitions P that are observationally equivalent on X.
